name: Can you build an attached in-law suite on a small lot in Glendale or Burbank?

mainEntity.name: Can you build an attached in-law suite on a small lot in Glendale or Burbank?
mainEntity.text: Can you build an attached in-law suite on a small lot in Glendale or Burbank?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached in-law suite can often work on a small lot, but the design has to fit the site instead of forcing a large addition onto it. On compact Glendale and Burbank lots, setbacks, lot coverage, side-yard width, and access to the rear yard can determine whether the suite should be attached, partially attached, or built as an interior conversion. Detached units may still be possible, but they often lose out to space constraints. The smartest next step is a site feasibility review that checks dimensions, utilities, grading, and where the entrance could go. A good design team will test multiple options before settling on one plan. On small lots, the most successful projects usually prioritize efficient layout, natural light, privacy, and compliance over maximum square footage.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but small lots usually make attached in-law suites more challenging because setbacks, fire separation, parking, and utility routing can limit the layout. In many cases, a compact attached addition or interior conversion is more realistic than a large detached unit. The feasibility depends on lot coverage, existing house footprint, and local zoning rules.
